Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] AVideo YPTSocket plugin XSS injection via webSocketSelfURI/page_title query strings · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35: WWBN AVideo: Unauthenticated Stored DOM C
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
AVideo YPTSocket plugin XSS injection via webSocketSelfURI/page_title query strings AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated exploitation of GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 in WWBN AVideo by detecting HTTP requests to the YPTSocket token endpoint or WebSocket upgrade carrying HTML/JS payloads in the webSocketSelfURI or page_title query parameters. The payload is then broadcast to any admin viewing a page that renders the YPTSocket debug panel. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint path /plugin/YPTSocket/ and the two attacker-controlled parameters (webSocketSelfURI, page_title) named in functions.php:21-24 and MessageSQLiteV2.php:91/110, combined with URL-encoded and raw HTML/JS payload tokens (including the article's String.fromCharCode evasion). Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory text and the AVideo repo paths cited in the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 • https://github.com/WWBN/AVideo
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal QA/security teams pentesting the YPTSocket plugin (legitimate XSS test payloads)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Burp Suite, Nuclei, ZAP) probing AVideo with HTML/JS canary payloads
  • Bug-bounty researchers replaying the PoC against staging
  • Legitimate AVideo dashboards passing rich page titles that happen to contain '<' (rare — utf8_encode source values normally don't carry HTML)
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("Burp", "Nuclei", "ZAP", "sqlmap", "nikto") and SrcIp !in ("<internal_pentest_ranges>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull all hits on /plugin/YPTSocket/getWebSocket.json.php and the WebSocket upgrade with these parameters in the last 48h; URL-decode the query string and identify the actual JS payload, source IP, and User-Agent. Confirm whether the AVideo instance has the YPTSocket plugin enabled and debugSocket=true (the vulnerable default). Step 2 — Contain: block the offending source IP at the WAF/edge, disable the YPTSocket plugin or set debugSocket=false until patched (upgrade composer:WWBN/AVideo above 29.0), and force-rotate admin session cookies and CSRF tokens for any admin who was logged in during the window. Step 3 — Hunt: review admin-context API calls (user/role mutations, password changes, plugin enable/disable, content edits) from admin session IDs that overlap with the broadcast window; pivot on AdminUser browser sessions to outbound exfil to attacker-controlled domains in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("webSocketSelfURI=", "page_title=")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("%3Cimg", "%3Cscript", "onerror%3D", "onload%3D", "%3Csvg", "javascript%3A", "String.fromCharCode", "%3Ciframe", "<img", "<script", "onerror=", "onload=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectTokens = dynamic(["%3Cimg","%3Cscript","onerror%3D","onload%3D","%3Csvg","javascript%3A","String.fromCharCode","%3Ciframe","<img","<script","onerror=","onload=","fromCharCode"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
    | where (csUriQuery has "webSocketSelfURI=" or csUriQuery has "page_title=")
    | where csUriQuery has_any (SuspectTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsUriStem has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
    | where (CsUriQuery has "webSocketSelfURI=" or CsUriQuery has "page_title=")
    | where CsUriQuery has_any (SuspectTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=CsHost, SrcIp=CIp, Method=CsMethod, Uri=strcat(CsUriStem,"?",CsUriQuery), Status=ScStatus, UserAgent=UserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
    | where RequestURL has_any ("webSocketSelfURI=","page_title=")
    | where RequestURL has_any (SuspectTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DestinationHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Reporting from Vegas: Networking, AI, and good boys
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos weekly prevalent malware SHA256 IOC sweep (Coinminer / Procpatcher / KMS activator) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Talos weekly prevalent malware SHA256 IOC sweep (Coinminer / Procpatcher / KMS activator) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts process executions and file writes matching the five SHA256 hashes Talos called out as the week's most prevalent malware in their 2026-06-04 newsletter telemetry roundup. Covers Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (sample.exe), W32.C0AD494457-95 (f_000b97.html), and PUA.Win.Tool.Kmsactivator (AutoPico.exe). Rationale: Detection is grounded on the five SHA256 hashes Talos explicitly named in the 'Most prevalent malware files' block (VID001.exe Coinminer, sample.exe Procpatcher, f_000b97.html W32.C0AD494457-95, AutoPico.exe Kmsactivator, plus the fifth truncated entry). These are confirmed-bad per Talos detection names — file-reputation match is the highest-fidelity signal possible from this article. No external sources cross-checked: the IOC list is a weekly Talos telemetry snapshot from today's date with no second source yet published.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analysts intentionally detonating samples in a sandbox / malware-analysis VM (especially analysts retrieving Talos-flagged hashes for testing)
  • AutoPico.exe / KMS activator hash firing on unlicensed Windows installs (common in test/lab environments and unmanaged dev boxes)
  • f_000b97.html cached in browser cache directories from a benign visit — file write triggers without execution (review FolderPath for browser cache paths before escalating)
  • EDR vendor sample-collection / threat intel platforms (CrowdStrike, MDE attack surface reduction telemetry) pulling sample copies for analysis
  • Legitimate AV scanners writing the sample to quarantine — initiating process being the AV engine itself
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !contains "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !contains "\\Sandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","CSFalconService.exe","SenseIR.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the matching event's FolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, and AccountName. If folder is a known sandbox/quarantine path (e.g. C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine, sandbox VM paths) or parent is an AV engine, downgrade. Confirm the Talos detection name from the case statement against the article's labelling. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR network containment. Kill the live process tree; quarantine the file. For Coinminer (VID001.exe) check for persistence via Run keys and scheduled tasks; for Procpatcher review which process was patched (often AV/EDR tampering). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName to find the delivery vector (browser download? email attachment? USB?). Sweep the rest of the fleet for the same SHA256 over 30 days and for the parent's hash. If KMS activator triggered, audit the host for other PUA / cracked software via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory.
let TalosMalwareHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f","c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe","afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (TalosMalwareHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Source = "DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (TalosMalwareHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
              ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ParentCmd = "",
              Source = "DeviceFileEvents";
union ProcHits, FileHits

    SHA256 == "9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe)",

    SHA256 == "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "Talos prevalent (unspecified)",

| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("144.31.221.82") or RemoteUrl has_any ("kongtuke.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["144.31.221.82"]);

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Miasma npm Supply Chain Attack: Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp

StepSecurity
2026-06-04 5 use cases 3 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

self-replicating worm is spreading across the npm registry using binding.gyp, a file that triggers code execution during npm install without touching package.json scripts. The attack bypasses conventional security tools and has already compromised dozens of packages across multiple maintainer accounts.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma npm Supply Chain Attack: Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path · [LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path AICommand & Control High
Hunts the specific KongTuke (TAG-124 / 404 TDS) command-and-control infrastructure named in the Talos case study: outbound HTTP to 144.31.221.82 on TCP/6060 with a URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint. Single-IOC alerting because all three values are article-named. Rationale: Single high-confidence IOC bundle straight from the Talos case-study paragraph: IP 144.31.221.82, TCP/6060, URL path /capcha9856. The /capcha* fingerprint is corroborated by Recorded Future (TAG-124), Red Canary KongTuke profile, and malware-traffic-analysis.net Jan 2026 KongTuke ClickFix capture. Cross-checked via WebSearch — KongTuke is a real, active TDS. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base • https://www.malware-traffic-analysis.net/2026/01/08/index.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentest or red-team rehearsal targeting the same IOC after reading the Talos blog
  • Threat-intel platform or DFIR sandbox automatically dialling out to known-bad C2 for verification (e.g. JoeSandbox, ANY.RUN agent on a corp jump host)
  • Threat-hunt tooling that replays packet captures with the destination IP rewritten for test purposes
  • Security awareness training simulator using captured KongTuke traffic
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smss.exe","wininit.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","sbox","detonation","malsandbox"))
Response runbook
Triage: Confirm the source host is a real production endpoint, then pull DeviceProcessEvents on it for ±30 min around the connection. Look for cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → curl.exe chain that Talos documented. Check Defender/AMP for any blocked-detection signatures on the same host. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender for Endpoint / Falcon Network Containment. Block 144.31.221.82 + the /capcha URL pattern at the firewall and proxy. Force-reset the logged-in user's credentials. Hunt: Sweep the entire estate for any other endpoint connecting to 144.31.221.82, port 6060, or any URL containing /capcha. Check WordPress/CMS site referrer logs for which compromised site redirected the user (TDS chains). Submit the IP to TI vendors and enrol the URL-path pattern into the proxy as a hunt rule.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
   or RemoteUrl has "/capcha9856"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Cisco" or DeviceProduct has "Firepower" or DeviceProduct has "Secure Firewall" or isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
   or RequestURL has "/capcha9856"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort,
          RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: KongTuke TDS C2 to 144.31.221.82 / capcha URL Path
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a01
description: Detects outbound network traffic to KongTuke TDS C2 infrastructure (144.31.221.82:6060) or any URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint reported by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
  - https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '144.31.221.82'
  selection_port_path:
    DestinationPort: 6060
    DestinationHostname|contains: '/capcha'
  selection_path:
    Url|contains: '/capcha9856'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_port_path or selection_path
falsepositives:

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:cisco-firepower OR source:cisco_secure_firewall) AND (@DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 OR (@DestinationPort:6060 AND @DestinationHostname:*\/capcha*) OR @network.destination.ip:144.31.221.82 OR @url:*\/capcha9856*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82" OR RemotePort=6060)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/capcha/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName], mode=left)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])

PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the KongTuke stage-2 download pattern from the Talos case study: a powershell.exe process whose command line invokes Invoke-WebRequest (or iwr) and writes a file named script.ps1 into the user's ApplicationData / AppData directory. Pairs the URL-fetch verb, the article-named filename, and the article-named drop location in one event. Rationale: The combination of three article-named tokens in one PowerShell command line — Invoke-WebRequest verb, exact filename script.ps1, and AppData/ApplicationData drop path — collapses to one cmdline-substring detection that's high specificity. Sourced directly from the Talos KongTuke walk-through (cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → IWR → script.ps1 → ApplicationData). Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin debugging an internal PowerShell module by manually fetching a generic 'script.ps1' into AppData
  • Software install wrapper that downloads a setup script (rename script.ps1 → install.ps1 is more common, but some installers do this)
  • Red-team / atomic-red-team test cases that mirror the KongTuke download chain
  • Security researcher rehydrating IOCs in a lab VM joined to corporate Defender
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("vscode.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sbx","sandbox","redteam","atomic"))
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the parent process tree for the powershell.exe event — confirm parent is cmd.exe spawned from a browser process (chrome/edge/firefox), which matches the TDS-redirect chain. Decode any preceding -EncodedCommand on the same PID. Hash and submit the dropped script.ps1 (still in %AppData%) to sandbox; capture content before Remove-Item runs. Contain: Isolate the host. Suspend the affected user account. Block C2 144.31.221.82 + /capcha pattern at egress. Hunt: Sweep estate for any powershell.exe with script.ps1 + AppData in cmdline. Pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for that PID/host and confirm C2 callback. Pull browser history for the user to find the compromised WordPress redirector that launched the TDS chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr ", "Net.WebClient", "DownloadFile", "DownloadString")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "script.ps1"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AppData", "ApplicationData", "\\Roaming\\", "\\Local\\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"

title: KongTuke PowerShell Drops script.ps1 to AppData via Invoke-WebRequest
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a02
description: Detects PowerShell command line that fetches a remote file named script.ps1 and writes it into the user's AppData directory — the KongTuke stage-2 download chain documented by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_fetch:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'DownloadString'
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains: 'script.ps1'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'AppData'
      - 'ApplicationData'
      - '\Roaming\'
      - '\Local\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal scripts that happen to fetch a file named script.ps1 into AppData (rare; review user context)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (@CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *iwr\ * OR *Net.WebClient* OR *DownloadFile* OR *DownloadString*)) AND @CommandLine:*script.ps1* AND (@CommandLine:(*AppData* OR *ApplicationData* OR *\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Local\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|iwr |Net\.WebClient|DownloadFile|DownloadString)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("script\.ps1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(AppData|ApplicationData|\\\\Roaming\\\\|\\\\Local\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window AICommand & Control High
Reproduces the Talos multi-source-correlation insight: the same endpoint reaching 144.31.221.82 from two distinct binaries (powershell.exe via Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe directly) is the disambiguating signal that turned a single firewall hit into a confirmed intrusion. Single-binary callouts to the IP are already caught by UC1; this UC fires on the host-level fan-out only. Rationale: Directly encodes the Talos case-study insight: 'a separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Two distinct LOLBin/native binaries calling the same KongTuke IP from one host is high-fidelity even without the URL-path filter — it's the multi-process fan-out that confirms intrusion vs single-shot scanning. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT troubleshooting a connectivity issue, running both Test-NetConnection (PowerShell) and curl against the same external host
  • Monitoring agents (e.g. uptime checks) that issue parallel HTTP probes from multiple wrappers
  • Red-team simulation reproducing the Talos case study against the same IOCs
  • Custom CMDB sync script that uses both powershell IWR and curl for redundancy
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("ops-","jumpbox-","netops-")) and not (AccountName has_any ("netops","sre","itadmin"))
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the process trees for both the powershell.exe and curl.exe events — confirm common parent or temporal proximity (<10 min). Decode any -EncodedCommand on the powershell side; capture curl.exe full command-line (URL, headers, output path). Verify the destination IP/path against KongTuke IOC list. Contain: Isolate the host. Force a credential reset for the logged-in user. Block 144.31.221.82 + /capcha pattern at proxy and firewall. Snapshot the host for memory analysis before reimage. Hunt: Run UC1 + UC2 across the estate to find any other host hitting KongTuke. Pivot on the IP via VirusTotal / Shodan for sibling infrastructure; add ASN to network-egress hunt block. Check email gateway for any KongTuke-themed lure URL that arrived in the 24h before first observation.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82" or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe")
| summarize ProcessSet = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            FirstConnection = min(Timestamp),
            LastConnection = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            CmdLines = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 8)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(ProcessSet) >= 2
| where (ProcessSet has "curl.exe") and (ProcessSet has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| order by FirstConnection desc
let WindowHours = 1h;
let FirewallHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82" or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
    | project FirewallTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL;
let ProcessHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("144.31.221.82", "capcha", "script.ps1")
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | project ProcessTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName;
FirewallHits
| join kind=inner (
    ProcessHits
    | summarize Procs=make_set(NewProcessName), AnyCmd=make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer
    | where array_length(Procs) >= 2
) on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| order by FirewallTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\Curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82"
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[collect([ContextImageFileName]), count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
| length(ContextImageFileName) >= 2

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Node-gyp Supply Chain Compromise: A Self-Propagating npm Worm That Hides in binding.gyp

Snyk
2026-06-04 7 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

A new npm worm is abusing binding.gyp to trigger node-gyp during install, letting malicious packages run code without lifecycle scripts. It steals credentials, persists in GitHub, and self-propagates across maintainers.

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Node-gyp Supply Chain Compromise: A Self-Propagating npm Worm That Hides in bind
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
